title: Cardinal Morosini, nuncio and legate in France, to Rome, 1587-89: 35 cipher enclosures in Meister's key no. 40 (AAV Segr. Stato Francia 22, DECODE R18-R22, R27-R49, R51, R52, R55-R58; Francia 18/3, DECODE R17)

documents.shelfmark: AAV Segr. Stato Francia 22, items 22/1-28, 22/30-31, 22/34-37 (DECODE R18-R22, R27-R49, R51, R52, R55-R58)

plaintext.source: No decipherment found; clear duplicates of the covering letters only (R18/R19 DOC_1806/1807). No edition of Morosini's legation found (searched 19 Sept 2026).

transcription.source: DECODE volunteer transcriptions (2017), digit by digit
transcription.notes: Count is single digits, not code groups: the 1-3 digit homophones run on without separators, so group count depends on the segmentation. Off-list dotted codes are thought to be transcription slips, not checked against images. Measured on the concatenation of decode/DOC_R*_D16xx-D18xx.txt (37 files for 34 records, D1806/D1807 clear duplicates excluded) with --width 1.

documents.shelfmark: ASV Segr. Stato Francia 18/3, ff. 233-235 (DECODE R17)

transcription.notes: Used as found; single digits counted (--width 1). Moved here from bergamo1585 on 14 Oct 2026.

system.summary: Meister no. 40 (1587): homophonic letters, clusters and common words in 1-3 digit figures run together without separators, three-digit dotted nomenclator, nulls 8x.

diacritics.note: dot on the middle digit marks a nomenclator code

system.sibling_key: none used (R53/R54 of the same volume are in a second key, F22b: targets/morosini1589)
system.notes: Decoded by beam search over segmentations scored with the shared it-cinquecento 5-gram model (decrypt.py). Null rule: 8 plus any following digit.

prior_solution.where: Key printed in Meister, Die Geheimschrift im Dienste der paepstlichen Kurie (1906) no. 40; Lasry's partial reconstruction on DECODE R18 (DOC_3175, Oct 2020) with the note 'full key in Meister'; no plaintext posted, records listed 'partially decrypted'. R17's DECODE note names the same Meister key; its decryption file is a Java error trace.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code and posed the problem; no target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched the DECODE records R18-R58 (transcriptions, images, attached key documents); identified R23-R26 and R50 as other material.
Took the key from Meister 1906 no. 40 (scan and Lasry's reconstruction attached to R18).
Wrote decrypt.py: beam search over 1-3 digit segmentations with the Italian 5-gram model, nomenclator for dotted codes.
Read the 34 Meister-key enclosures of Francia 22 end to end; per-item summaries written.
R17 (Francia 18/3, filed with the Bergamo/Nazareth despatches) decrypted with Meister no. 40 via decrypt.py: all five pages, 5 unknown codes; a Morosini-period despatch of 1587.
Searched for an edition of the legation (Acta Nuntiaturae Gallicae); none found.

Split under the one-key rule: R53/R54 (second key F22b) moved to their own entry morosini1589; R17 moved in from bergamo1585 (same key); measure.py counts the 35 Meister-key records: 134,010 units, 195 unread (0.9985).

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): per enclosure, DECODE's cipher transcription (decode/DOC_R*_D16xx/17xx) and the word-split decoder output copied from decode_updates/decryptions into texts/; R17 transcription, decryption and word-split files. Lasry's partial key is decode/DOC_R18_D3175_3175.txt; the full key is Meister's, in decrypt.py.

outcome.method_basis: Meister 1906 no. 40, the key printed for Morosini's nunciature, with Lasry's partial reconstruction attached to DECODE R18 before the attempt, read all 35 enclosures in that key (34 in Francia 22 and R17 in Francia 18); unseparated 1-3 digit homophones were segmented by a beam search with an Italian 5-gram model.

gaps.item: dotted nomenclator codes outside Meister's list (162, 191, 250, 516, 617, 716, 770; ~1 per page)
gaps.detail: most look like transcription slips of a dotted digit; not checked against the images
no DECODE record; not imaged; its key is not known
Meister no. 40 reads all five pages except these; most likely transcription slips, images not re-read

outcome.notes: Split 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): the two F22b enclosures R53/R54 are now morosini1589; R17 (Francia 18/3, read 21 Sept 2026 in bergamo1585) moved here, same key. Measured 14 Oct 2026: 0.998 of units have a value over the 35 records; codes_open counts the five R17 codes (the off-list dotted codes of Francia 22 are thought to be transcription slips, not counted).

credits.note: Die Geheimschrift (1906) no. 40, key issued to Morosini 1587, applied to the 34 Francia 22 enclosures and R17
credits.source: A. Meister, Die Geheimschrift im Dienste der päpstlichen Kurie (Paderborn 1906) pp. 393-394, no. 40

credits.note: partial key reconstruction on DECODE R18 (DOC_3175, Oct 2020), with the note 'full key in Meister'; his F22b key is credited on morosini1589

outcome.fraction_read_source: targets/morosini1588/measure.py over decrypt_raw.txt (34 Francia 22 records) and R17_decryption.txt: units = decoded letters + bracketed nomenclator groups; unread = '?' letters and '[nnn?]' groups (195 of 134,010). Single-letter slips that decode to a wrong letter (1-3 per hundred by eye) are not counted.

texts.label: R18, Francia 22/1, 10 Aug [1588] (duplicate)
texts.summary: On publishing the Council of Trent: strong resistance everywhere over Gallican liberties. In Paris Morosini lobbied the Sorbonne and the royal council, and told Henri III that a Most Christian king should accept the council without conditions. The King answered that the clergy, above all the Archbishop of Lyon, were the ones opposing it.

texts.label: R19, Francia 22/2, 24 Aug [1588] (duplicate)
texts.summary: The clergy's deputies appeared before the Parlement to oppose the council as against Gallican liberty. In an audience the King defended his privileges and benefice nominations. He was told that the legation's faculties must be verified by the Parlement.

texts.label: R20, Francia 22/3, 9 Sept [1588]
texts.summary: The King gave the Count of Soissons letters clearing him of his service with Navarre and the Huguenots. Paris citizens and the prévôt protested to the Parlement. Cardinal de Vendôme and the Princess of Condé were furious.

texts.label: R21, Francia 22/4, n.d. [Sept 1588]
texts.summary: The King dismissed his secretaries of state and the chancellor all at once, leaving the court anxious. Mons. de Nevers(?) and the Queen Mother were displeased not to have been consulted. Morosini warned the King that new men would be inexperienced and the old ones could side with his enemies.

texts.label: R22, Francia 22/5, n.d. [Sept 1588] (duplicate)
texts.summary: Replies to Montalto. Morosini has kept pressing for the council; the Estates promise to ask for it. His faculties will not be obeyed unless the Parlement verifies them.

texts.label: R27, Francia 22/6, n.d. (fragment)
texts.summary: On governments for Épernon (Saintonge, Angoulême, Cognac) and on Boulogne. Épernon's side refuses to give anything back and is said to deal with the Queen of England and Navarre. Morosini hopes for peace between Guise and the others, though with little confidence.

texts.label: R28, Francia 22/7, [early] Oct [1588] (duplicate)
texts.summary: While walking in the palace garden with the King, the Queen Mother and the Cardinals of Bourbon and Vendôme, Morosini learned that the King would send Signor Girolamo Gondi to Rome about pulling Marshal Montmorency away from the Huguenots. Morosini urged the King to win Guise over with money, since Guise is heavily in debt; Guise refused the grant offered. Vendôme reports that Cardinal Joyeuse worked against the Count of Soissons in Rome.

texts.label: R29, Francia 22/8, 10 Oct [1588] (duplicate)
texts.summary: A messenger is back from Florence about the Grand Duke's marriage to the Princess of Lorraine; Orazio Rucellai will conclude it, and the Queen Mother plans to escort her to Marseille. News that the Duke of Savoy has seized the whole marquisate of Saluzzo; Guise fears this will force peace with Navarre and the heretics. Morosini asks for orders; a Danish ambassador is dealing over merchants' goods.

texts.label: R30, Francia 22/9, 3 Oct [1588], Blois
texts.summary: Morosini took on the job of reconciling the Duke of Guise and Mons. de Nevers, who have been at odds since they married sisters; with the King's approval, both promised to follow his advice. He pressed Guise and the Cardinal of Guise on publishing the council. The clergy is split: the lower deputies want Gallican liberty reserved.

texts.label: R31, Francia 22/10, 23 Oct [1588], Blois
texts.summary: Mandelot, governor of Lyon, is ordered to arrest a man for transfer to Avignon. The Cardinal of Guise asks for the vice-legation of Avignon. The Florentine marriage contract is going forward.

texts.label: R32, Francia 22/11, 24 Oct [1588]
texts.summary: Savoy is keeping Saluzzo and is suspected of designs on Marseille. M. de Poigny is sent to the Duke to demand restitution. Morosini protests over Cardinal Lenoncourt's indult and over church revenues in the Cambrai truce, and the Queen Mother answers him.

texts.label: R33, Francia 22/12, n.d. [Oct-Nov 1588]
texts.summary: The King referred the council to the clergy's congregation. There the chapters, bishops and others quarrelled over exemptions, and they finally asked for publication with four reservations (royal authority, Gallican liberty, chapter exemptions, particular privileges). Morosini argued that it must be published without conditions.

texts.label: R34, Francia 22/13, n.d. [Nov 1588]
texts.summary: The Spanish ambassador pressed the Queen Mother for union and good understanding between Philip II and Henri III, and showed a copy of Philip's letter. Morosini sees a real opening for the alliance and asks that it be kept secret. The ambassador blamed Savoy for the Saluzzo attack.

texts.label: R35, Francia 22/14, n.d.
texts.summary: A copy, in Spanish, of Philip II's letter to the Queen Mother (given to her by the Spanish ambassador). It urges closer union and friendship between the two crowns against the heretics, for God's service and obedience to the Roman Church.

texts.label: R36, Francia 22/15, 10 Nov [1588] (duplicate)
texts.summary: A fever kept Morosini indoors. The Savoy ambassador reported the Poigny talks to the Queen Mother: the Duke will not return the Saluzzo places, and claims to have acted by the Pope's order (Carmagnola). Morosini firmly denies that the Pope had any part in it.

texts.label: R37, Francia 22/16, 21 Nov [1588] (duplicate)
texts.summary: Morosini urged the King and Queen Mother to settle Saluzzo peacefully. The Savoy ambassador had offered to restore the places if they were given to a Catholic knight, with Nemours as governor. Guise advised force instead, sending Mayenne into Bresse.

texts.label: R38, Francia 22/17, n.d. [late Nov-Dec 1588]
texts.summary: The Savoy ambassador complained that Mayenne was ordered into Bresse. Morosini urged the King not to start a war before trying every other way, and to fight the heretics first. The King said he gave Mayenne no such order, but called the Duke of Savoy ungrateful.

texts.label: R39, Francia 22/18, 8 Dec [1588] (duplicate)
texts.summary: A courier from Turin came from Poigny. In the council, Nevers insisted on war with Savoy even if Saluzzo were restored; the others would forgive the Duke if he gave the places back. Munitions and artillery are to be sent to Lyon.

texts.label: R40, Francia 22/19, dup., "li 8 X[bre]" (8 Dec 1588?), [Blois]
texts.summary: The King's council discusses the Duke of Savoy's artillery and troops on the borders of Bresse and Dauphiné and resolves to levy Swiss and 1,500 horse to join the Duke of Mayenne; the Duke of Guise offers 10,000 scudi, and the Estates' treasurers promise money. Morosini goes to the Capuchins hoping to find Henri III and complains that the King no longer talks openly with him. He reports that the King is tightly bound to Guise and is said to have dismissed his heads of finance.

texts.label: R41, Francia 22/20, n.d. [Blois, Dec 1588]
texts.summary: The Duke of Savoy has seized the Marquisate of Saluzzo and offers to give it back once the Dauphiné is free of Huguenots, with his wife or a son as a hostage. The Duke of Guise tells Morosini he must press the King to recover Saluzzo by force, or else retire from court; the Savoyard ambassador has been refused. Mayenne asks what to do, with the Savoyard enemy so near.

texts.label: R42, Francia 22/21, n.d. [Blois, Dec 1588]
texts.summary: Morosini tells the King at the Capuchins that the Pope is displeased the Council of Trent has not been published; the King answers through Gondi. Guise complains that the King does not trust him, and Morosini urges the King to satisfy Guise. He also reports on the papal bull against procurers of abortion and says the Queen Mother has a fever.

texts.label: R43, Francia 22/22, Blois, 23 Dec [1588]
texts.summary: Guise is killed with daggers in the King's chamber on the King's order, after warnings that he meant harm to the King. The Cardinal of Guise, the Prince de Joinville, the Dukes of Nemours and Elbeuf, the Archbishop of Lyon, the prévôt des marchands and a Paris president are arrested, and the Cardinal de Bourbon is put under guard. The Queen Mother is left speechless, the city is locked down, Morosini seeks an audience in vain, and the Cardinal of Guise is feared dead too.

texts.label: R44, Francia 22/23, dup., 24 Xbre [1588], [Blois]
texts.summary: The Cardinal of Guise was put to death only this morning. Because he was a churchman, Morosini leaves the response to the Pope's judgment. The Cardinal de Bourbon is under guard and ill, and Joinville and the Archbishop of Lyon are to go to Amboise.

texts.label: R45, Francia 22/24, n.d. [Blois, Jan 1589, after Catherine de' Medici's death]
texts.summary: Morosini defends his conduct. The Archbishop of Lyon refuses lay examiners because he is primate of France. The Estates' article excluding Navarre carries a clause reserving the Bourbon succession.

texts.label: R46, Francia 22/25, Blois, 24 Jan 1589 (dup.)
texts.summary: The Pope rejects the clause "saluis iuribus regis et regni", and Morosini works on the King's confessor and the Keeper of the Seals, who promise to argue his case. Saluzzo is set aside for now. At length Morosini complains of the Pope's displeasure and the false reports reaching Rome, and he begs leave to come to Rome to justify himself.

texts.label: R47, Francia 22/26, n.d. [Blois, Jan 1589]
texts.summary: Morosini continues his defence and denies ever dealing with the English ambassador. He explains why the Council could not be forced through the parlements and the Estates. He had suggested that the King publish it at once and then send a personage to Rome to ask for his privileges.

texts.label: R48, Francia 22/27, Blois, 30 & 31 Jan 1589
texts.summary: Morosini again asks for his leave. The Parisians have put themselves under Mayenne's protection, and the King is leaving for Amboise with his prisoners. Morosini protests about moving the Cardinal de Bourbon and the Archbishop of Lyon.

texts.label: R49, Francia 22/28, n.d. (fragment) [early 1589]
texts.summary: The Archbishop of Lyon refuses to answer the royal commissioners or a bishop, saying he is primate of France. His relatives ask Morosini to plead with the King not to prejudice ecclesiastical dignity and to refer the case to the Pope.

texts.label: R51, Francia 22/30, Tours, 27 March 1589
texts.summary: A count's gentleman brings news that two cavalry companies of Mayenne's (under Sagona and Farlandra, who was badly wounded) have been routed and their baggage taken. Orléans and Paris are in the League's hands, and Mayenne remains in Paris. The King wants peace, while Navarre is taking places.

texts.label: R52, Francia 22/31, Tours, 6 April 1589
texts.summary: The castellan of Angers refuses the League's bribe, and Marshal d'Aumont secures the castle for the King, who writes him a letter in his own hand. The count is sent to Brittany against the Duke of Mercoeur; Alfonso Corso is in Auvergne; Épernon's command is disputed; Mayenne is still in Paris. The King keeps Holy Week and Easter devotions and touches for the scrofula.

texts.label: R55, Francia 22/34, Moulins, 11 June 1589
texts.summary: A gentleman of the Grand Duchess of Tuscany reports that the Comte de Soissons (?) was captured in bed by the Duke of Mercoeur, and that a League count was killed by a gunpowder explosion. The King is marching on Paris, where Mayenne is and the city is barricaded, with 4,000 horse and 17,000 foot; Swiss and Casimir's cavalry are coming, and Épernon has taken Montereau. Morosini also passes on, with doubts, a rumour of a plot to kill the King.

texts.label: R56, Francia 22/35, Moulins, 16(?) June 1589
texts.summary: Morosini is distressed by Montalto's letter about his secretary. The monitorium has reportedly been posted at St Peter's, and Cardinal Joyeuse and the French ambassador are leaving Rome. Morosini thinks of retiring to Lyon, but the Lyonnais will let him stay only three days.

texts.label: R57, Francia 22/36, n.d. (enclosures dated "dix di giugno" [1589], Moulins)
texts.summary: This record holds copies of papers sent to M. de la Guiche. The first says the King's Swiss army (about 12,000 Swiss and 2,000 lansquenets, some 17–18,000 men with 12 guns) is marching, paid with money lent by Strasbourg. The second is the oath of the inhabitants of Moulins to live and die Catholic and loyal to "Henri, by the grace of God King of France and Poland".

texts.label: R58, Francia 22/37, Moulins, 5 July 1589 (dup.)
texts.summary: The King has taken Jargeau ("Giorgio") and its Loire bridge, hanged a captain and pardoned the governor. Other Loire towns have surrendered, and the King is heading for Paris, where four faubourgs are said to favour him. Mayenne has taken Montereau and Nemours is raising money at Lyon for the League's Swiss.

texts.label: R17, Francia 18/3, ff. 233r-235v, 1587
texts.summary: A Morosini-period letter of 1587 in the Meister no. 40 key, filed by DECODE with the Bergamo/Nazareth despatches: it concerns the Duke of Lorraine and Guise, the German reiters, the Queen Mother and Schomberg.
